input.trigger: coordinator-relayed independent code review P1: symlink traversal in the workflow context assembly
input.confirmed_defect: shutil.copytree(source_crate/'src', ...) and shutil.copy2(...) follow links by default and write target content as ordinary files, so a benign-named link can smuggle retired game/legacy payload into the context under a path that every name-based gate accepts; reproduced locally with a junction whose copied output vendor/lib.rs contained the smuggle marker
second_order_findings: Windows directory junction reports is_symlink()=False and os.path.islink()=False while Path.is_junction()=True, and copytree still follows it, so a symlink-only check misses it entirely
an internal ancestor link (repo/crates -> repo/legacy-source) keeps realpath inside the checkout and exposes ordinary children to os.walk, so containment and traversal checks both pass
os.walk(followlinks=False) still descends into junctions on Windows
os.symlink on this machine raises OSError WinError 1314 (no privilege), so link fixtures must use junctions here
input.reviewer_followup: ancestor components between allowed_root and each source were initially not checked; fixed by inspecting every lexical path component before containment and copy

output.gate_position: one enforce() call placed before every copy2/copytree in the context assembly step
output.allowed_root_itself_excluded_from_link_c: yes; avoids false positives when the runner workspace sits behind a system symlink, containment is still enforced via realpath on both sides
output.pruning: directories that are links or whose realpath escapes are pruned in place, so a link aimed at a large tree cannot turn the gate into an unbounded scan
